evals.prompt: Can you harden this repo against AI slop? We've got a basic husky pre-commit that just runs prettier but nothing else right now, and no CI at all yet. It's a small internal service, not public.
evals.expected_output: Detects Node/TypeScript + Vitest + existing partial husky hook, presents the stack for confirmation, proposes extending the existing husky hook (not replacing it) with lint/type-check, plus a CI workflow, secret scanning, and dependency audit, tailored to a team-internal (not public) repo. Approval-gated before any file writes.
expectations: Presented the detected stack (Node.js/TypeScript, Vitest) for confirmation before writing any files
Identified the existing .husky/pre-commit hook and extended it rather than deleting/fully replacing it
The final .husky/pre-commit (or equivalent hook config) still runs prettier, not just newly added checks
Added a GitHub Actions CI workflow file under .github/workflows/
Proposed or added secret scanning (e.g. gitleaks or equivalent)
Scoped governance/tier proposals to a private/team-internal repo, not a public/OSS one
Added a provenance marker comment ('generated by codeguard') to newly created config files
Reported the environment as host machine / not in a container
Final summary explained how to bypass a hook in an emergency and how to undo the setup

evals.prompt: We haven't started building Recipe Vault yet, just have the PRD and architecture docs in docs/_bmad-output/. Can you get the guardrails set up before we start writing any code?
evals.expected_output: Infers the intended stack (Python/FastAPI/SQLModel backend, React/Vite/TS frontend, uv + pnpm) from docs/_bmad-output/prd.md and architecture.md rather than asking the user cold, presents it for confirmation, and proposes a plan appropriate for a personal/greenfield project with no code yet.
expectations: Inferred the intended stack from docs/_bmad-output/, without asking the user cold for the stack
Explicitly cited docs/_bmad-output/prd.md and/or architecture.md as the source of the stack detection
Presented the detected stack for confirmation before proposing safeguards
Proposed a plan scoped to a project with no code yet, not a full heavy-governance suite for an empty repo
Wrote conventions into CLAUDE.md using the codeguard sentinel block, preserving existing content
Did not fabricate contact details in any generated governance file

evals.prompt: This FastAPI invoicing service has zero safeguards right now — no hooks, no CI, nothing. Set it up properly for a small internal team.
evals.expected_output: Detects Python/FastAPI/uv-appropriate stack, finds no existing safeguards, proposes a full tier-1/2/3 setup (ruff, mypy, pytest+coverage, pre-commit or lefthook, GitHub Actions CI, secret scanning, dependency audit) sized for a team-internal repo, gated on approval before writing.
expectations: Correctly detected Python/FastAPI as the stack
Proposed ruff for lint/format
Proposed and installed a git hook manager since none existed
Added a GitHub Actions CI workflow with lint/type-check/test jobs
Proposed or added secret scanning and a dependency audit step
Added a provenance marker comment to newly created config files
Scoped the proposal to a team-internal (not public) repo appropriately
Actually created the CI workflow file, hook config, and CLAUDE.md additions, not just described them
Presented the proposal and an approval gate before writing files
